_meta.indication: XURIDEN is indicated for the treatment of hereditary orotic aciduria.

pivotal_trials.trial_name: Study 001 (Protocol 401.13.001), "Open-Label Study of Uridine Triacetate in Pediatric Patients with Hereditary Orotic Aciduria"
pivotal_trials.phase: A single registration efficacy and safety trial
pivotal_trials.design: A 6-week open-label efficacy and safety trial followed by an extension trial of unspecified length, conducted at two US sites
pivotal_trials.population: Patients with hereditary orotic aciduria aged ≤19 years (3 previously treated with uridine, 1 treatment-naive), age range 3 to 19 years
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Stability (for patients switching from uridine) or improvement (for the treatment-naive patient) of patient-specific predetermined hematologic parameters (neutrophil count, white blood cell count, or mean corpuscular volume) at Days 28 and 42
pivotal_trials.n: 4 patients (all 4 completed the main treatment phase)
pivotal_trials.result: All three patients who transitioned from uridine maintained stable hematologic parameters after 6 weeks; no improvement in hematologic status was demonstrated in the treatment-naive patient. Hematologic parameters for all four patients continued to show stability or improvement during the 6-month extension period.

nct_ctgov.title: Open-Label Study of Uridine Triacetate in Pediatric Patients With Hereditary Orotic Aciduria

key_safety: No adverse reactions were reported with XURIDEN. Safety was assessed in 4 patients with hereditary orotic aciduria (ages 3 to 19 years) receiving 60 mg/kg once daily for six weeks and continuing at up to 120 mg/kg once daily for at least 9 months.
target_moa: Uridine triacetate is a pro-drug of uridine that forms uridine upon metabolism, providing uridine in the systemic circulation of patients with hereditary orotic aciduria (UMP synthase deficiency) who cannot synthesize adequate uridine; restoration of intracellular uridine nucleotides reduces overproduction of orotic acid by feedback inhibition.
modality: Small molecule (pyrimidine analog / pro-drug of uridine)

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee meeting was held for this application; the clinical program was designed with FDA input and no efficacy or safety issues were identified.

description.text: Labeling update to Clinical Studies with efficacy data on hematologic and growth parameters through 24 months of treatment; no new indication

citations.quote: This Prior Approval supplemental new drug application provides for labeling changes to update section 14 Clinical Studies of the Prescribing Information with efficacy data on hematologic and growth parameters through 24 months of treatment in Study 401-13-001.

basis.text: The Agency granted Breakthrough Product designation for uridine triacetate for HOA on April 25, 2014, based on clinical data from published case studies and clinical summaries for the expanded access INDs.

citations.quote: **April 25, 2014:** The Agency granted Breakthrough Product designation for uridine triacetate for HOA based on clinical data presented from published case studies and clinical summaries for the expanded access INDs.

orphan_indication.text: Uridine triacetate was granted orphan drug designation for the treatment of hereditary orotic aciduria (Orphan Product designation granted August 9, 2014).

citations.quote: Uridine triacetate was granted orphan drug designation for the treatment of hereditary orotic aciduria. Therefore, this application is exempt from the requirements of the Pediatric Research Equity Act (PREA).
**August 9, 2014:** The Agency granted Orphan Product designation for uridine triacetate for HOA.

summary.text: Xuriden (uridine triacetate) for hereditary orotic aciduria received Breakthrough Product designation (April 25, 2014) and Orphan Product designation (August 9, 2014). The NDA, received January 8, 2015, was approved September 4, 2015 based on a single open-label registration trial in 4 patients, with the sponsor granted a rare pediatric disease priority review voucher.

citations.quote: **April 25, 2014:** The Agency granted Breakthrough Product designation for uridine triacetate for HOA based on clinical data presented from published case studies and clinical summaries for the expanded access INDs.
**August 9, 2014:** The Agency granted Orphan Product designation for uridine triacetate for HOA.

We also inform you that you have been granted a rare pediatric disease priority review voucher, as provided under section 529 of the FDCA. This priority review voucher (PRV) has been assigned a tracking number, PRV NDA 208169. All correspondences related to this voucher should refer to this tracking number.

requirement.text: 2932-1: Continue to evaluate the long-term efficacy and safety of XURIDEN in patients currently enrolled in Protocol 401-13-001 every 6 months for a total duration of 2 years in an extension trial, collecting data on growth, hematologic indices, and urine biomarkers (orotic acid and orotidine).

citations.quote: 2932-1 Continue to evaluate the long-term efficacy and safety of XURIDEN (uridine triacetate) in patients currently enrolled in Protocol 401-13-001 every 6 months for a total duration of 2 years in an extension trial. The extension trial should collect data on growth, hematologic indices, and urine biomarkers (orotic acid and orotidine). Growth data should include height, weight, height velocity and weight

requirement.text: 2932-2: Develop a discriminating dissolution method, set acceptance criteria based on at least 5 commercial batches, determine particle size distribution of the final drug product and evaluate its impact on dissolution, and update the final drug product particle size specification and in-process controls.

citations.quote: 2932-2 Develop a discriminating dissolution method appropriate for the proposed product and set dissolution method acceptance criteria based on data from at least 5 commercial batches. Determine the particle size distribution of the final drug product and, using the updated dissolution method, evaluate the impact of the particle size distribution on dissolution. The studies should also include an evaluation of batches submitted in the application (e.g., W017891, W017893, W017895, W012785, and W021129). Based on findings from these studies, update the final drug product particle size specification and the in-process controls.
